# The vdom parent walks restart from the component itself at an ancestor with no parentId, and overflow the stack

## Context

Found by @neo-opus-grace while reviewing #18901: `createNeoInstance` with `parentId: undefined` ended in `RangeError` inside `GridBody.mergeIntoParentUpdate`. Reproduced in the unit tier on `dev@6d61d8a900`. A Component created with `parentId: undefined` keeps `undefined` (the config default `'document.body'` does not replace an explicit `undefined`), and for its child both walks throw:

```
mergeIntoParentUpdate() → RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
isParentUpdating()      → RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

## The Problem

`VdomLifecycle#isParentUpdating(parentId=this.parentId, resolve, distance=1)` and `#mergeIntoParentUpdate(parentId=this.parentId, distance=1)` walk up by recursing with `parent.parentId`. The default parameter is meant for the first call only. But a recursion that passes an ancestor's `undefined` takes the default again, restarts from the component's own `parentId`, and walks the same chain forever. Every update of a component below such an ancestor then throws, since `update()` calls `mergeIntoParentUpdate()` first.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs`: the two walks (`:749`, `:794`), and their callers in `updateVdom`'s path (`mergeIntoParentUpdate(parentId)`, then `isParentUpdating(parentId, resolve)`).
- A walk ends at `'document.body'` or at an id that resolves to no component. An `undefined` id is neither, because the default parameter turns it back into `this.parentId`.
- No other `src` method recurses with a `this`-derived default parameter.

## The Fix

Both walks pass the next id as `parent.parentId ?? null`. A `null` argument takes no default, resolves to no component, and ends the walk as a missing ancestor does today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With an ancestor whose `parentId` is `undefined`, both walks return `false` instead of throwing, witnessed by a unit arm that is red without the fix.
- [ ] The walks' behaviour for a normal chain is unchanged: the existing merge and collision specs stay green.

## Out of Scope

- Whether a Component may be created with `parentId: undefined` at all.
